chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what they voluntarily surrender of themselves.

key_terms.اسْتَحَلَّهُمْ: They made permissible for themselves / voluntarily yielded

ai.seo_question: What is the extent of Satan's authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's dominion over the *Mu'minin* is not inherent but contingent upon their voluntary compliance or neglect, distinguishing them from those who are fully surrendered to him. This conditional authority underscores the Shia theological emphasis on human agency (*ikhtiyar*) and the necessity of continuous vigilance (*muraqabah*) to prevent the slip into minor sins that grant Satan leverage. The narration serves as a practical guide for spiritual resilience, affirming that while Satan has a guaranteed share in those who heed him, he has no power over those who actively resist through faith and righteous action.
